subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future tense form.

A signboard was hanging there for the travellers indicating the directions.

options.text: A signboard had hung there for the travellers indicating the directions.
A signboard will be hanging there for the travellers indicating the directions.
A signboard has been hanging there for the travellers indicating the directions.
A signboard is found hanging there for the travellers indicating the directions.

solution:
The correct answer is "**A signboard will be hanging there for the travellers indicating the directions.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in past tense ("A signboard was hanging there").
 
• **So to express it in future tense we need to use the future form i.e. "will be hanging."**
 
• **"Will" is the auxiliary verb used to form the future tense in English.**
 
• **"Be" is the auxiliary verb used to form the passive voice in English, which is needed here because the subject of the sentence is the signboard**, not the travellers.
 
• The main verb "hang" remains in its base form because it is preceded by the auxiliary verbs "will" and "be."
 
• Thus, the sentence in future form will be :
 
 
• A signboard will be hanging there for the travellers indicating the directions.
 
 

​​Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 ("A signboard had hung there") expresses the past perfect tense, which indicates an action that was completed before another past action.
 
• Option 3 ("A signboard has been hanging there") expresses the present perfect continuous tense, which indicates an ongoing action that started in the past and continues up to the present. 
 
• Option 4 ("A signboard is found hanging there") uses the present tense.
